title: Recognition of the algebraic residue-triple colimit
statement: Let A be a local commutative ring, K a separable closure of its residue field, and C a henselian local A-algebra in an independent universe. Suppose A -> C is local and IndEtaleAcrossUniverses. Let q:C -> K be surjective, with kernel the maximal ideal of C and composite from A equal to A -> k -> K. Let (p,chi) be the residue point induced by this base field-valued map. Let c be any universal cocone of the etale residue-triple ring diagram over (A,p,K,chi). Let qA:c.pt -> K have on each coprojection the triple residue map, and rho:A -> c.pt agree with every triple structural map followed by its coprojection. There exists a ring equivalence e:C -> c.pt preserving the A-map and satisfying q composed with e inverse = qA. Furthermore every ring map f:c.pt -> C satisfying f rho = algebraMap A C and q f = qA equals e inverse. This is algebraic recognition only and contains no geometric neighbourhoods, geometric colimit, or comparison map g.

proof.text: Identify p with the closed point and its residue field with k. Transport the separable closure structure to its scheme residue field. Apply strictHenselization_triples and transport the resulting local henselian structure and residue map along colimit uniqueness to c.pt. The prescribed rho is local ind-etale and qA is surjective with maximal-ideal kernel.

At unequal universes, use the canonical ULift equivalences defining IndEtaleAcrossUniverses to transport to a common universe; carry the local structures and residue maps through these ring equivalences. Take the filtered etale presentation of each ind-etale map.

Apply map_into_henselian_colimit in both directions with the identity map on K, using q and qA to identify the maximal-ideal residue fields. Their maximal ideals lie over the base maximal ideal by locality; base residue compatibility follows from their prescribed composites. Uniqueness compared with identity maps proves both composites are identities and yields e. For any f in the conclusion, its residue equation forces the same maximal-ideal inverse image and residue map. The uniqueness part of the same mapping theorem gives f=e inverse.

theorem geometric_triples_algebra_recognition
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : Type u) [Field K]
    [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) K] [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) K]
    (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [HenselianLocalRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A C)]
    (hC : RingHom.IndEtaleAcrossUniverses (algebraMap A C))
    (q : C →+* K) (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (hker : RingHom.ker q = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal C)
    (hqa : q.comp (algebraMap A C) = (geometricTriplesBaseResidue A K).hom)
    (c : Cocone (etaleResidueTriplesRingDiagram A (geometricTriplesResiduePoint A K).1 K
      (geometricTriplesResiduePoint A K).2)) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (qA : c.pt ⟶ .of K)
    (hqA : ∀ t, c.ι.app t ≫ qA = geometricTriplesTripleResidue t)
    (ρ : A ⟶ c.pt) (hρ : ∀ t, t.α ≫ c.ι.app t = ρ) :
    ∃ e : C ≃+* c.pt,
      e.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap A C) = ρ.hom ∧
      q.comp e.symm.toRingHom = qA.hom ∧
      ∀ f : c.pt →+* C,
        f.comp ρ.hom = algebraMap A C → q.comp f = qA.hom →
        f = e.symm.toRingHom
